reason: Confirmed in-scope claim c1: per-bin, per-width comparison against the FP64 rfft reference on random FP16 inputs fails catastrophically at every legal width N in {64,128,256} — worst error/tolerance ratios 2.15e5 (N=64), 2.97e5 (N=128), 4.36e5 (N=256) — with no nonfinite output. The contract (problem.txt is the operative contract; no test.py/get_inputs narrowing) requires abs(actual-exact) <= 1e-4 + 1e-6*abs(exact) for the exact unnormalized real DFT; these violations are orders of magnitude beyond any rounding/representation tolerance the contract could account for, indicating a genuine sign/scaling/indexing error in the DIF butterfly or packed-to-real reconstruction. c2 (Nyquist-bin defect) is rebutted: the Nyquist bin matches exactly with exactly-zero imaginary part at all widths. c3 (extreme-magnitude cancellation tolerance) remains inconclusive solely because both probe attempts constructed illegal non-finite FP16 values (probe errors, not kernel defects); I set it aside because it cannot change the verdict already established by c1 and no evidence implicates a kernel defect there.
